## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Hetuduka* (Patthana 14.1) is a text belonging to the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final work of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Based on the Abhidhamma *mātikā*, the dyad categorizes phenomena into those that are root causes (*hetū dhammā*) and those that are not root causes (*na hetū dhammā*) [U Kyaw Khine 1999]. In the conditional methodology of the *Paṭṭhāna*, it examines causal conditioning between these categories, such as the arising of a not-root phenomenon dependent on a root phenomenon conditioned by root condition (*hetu-paccaya*) [Nyanatiloka 2007].
According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive Pali-internal text reuse reflecting the combinatorial nature of the *Paṭṭhāna*, sharing 417 passages with 65 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest text-reuse correspondences are with texts containing parallel permutations of the root dyad, including *Hetuduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.1; 78 matches), *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 65 matches), *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 25 matches), and *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1; 17 matches) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus records no cross-language alignments with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus].
